sections.visual_cue: Close‑up of 184 cuneiform tablets stacked, with a faint plague symbol overlay.

sections.voiceover: Archaeologists uncovered 184 cuneiform tablets at Samuha, an ancient Hittite settlement in Sivas, Turkey. What crisis does this archive reveal?
sections.visual_cue: Map of Turkey zooming to Sivas, then to Samuha site, followed by images of tablets and a portrait of King Tudhaliya II.

sections.voiceover: These 184 tablets reveal a deadly epidemic and military threats recorded at the Kayalıpınar site.
sections.visual_cue: Animated scene of ancient soldiers advancing toward Samuha, with a red plague cloud hovering above the city.

sections.voiceover: This 3,400-year-old archive details a Hittite empire pandemic; Çiğdem Maner's Koç University team unearthed these records. 184 tablets—131 from Tudhaliya II's reign—provide unprecedented detail on the crisis.
sections.visual_cue: Timeline graphic showing 3,400 years, split‑screen of ritual scenes and tablets, highlighting the numbers 184 and 131.

sections.voiceover: A hidden plague revealed by 184 tablets.
sections.visual_cue: Fade to a single tablet with the number 184 embossed.
